Fermentists of Origin™ Bioactive by Design™ Investor dossier · Aug 2026

The problem

Specialty coffee is a retail business dressed as a craft one.

The industry's premium tier buys green beans it did not grow, applies heat it did not design, and sells the result as craft. The actual chemistry — what happens inside the cherry, before anyone lights a roaster — is left to chance.

Processing loses bioactives

Conventional processing and roasting degrade a substantial share of green-bean compounds — chlorogenic acids and trigonelline chief among them.

Premium without engineering

A café that sources a washed lot and roasts it well has added craft, not chemistry. The compound profile it sells is the one it received.

No one measures the cup

Specialty grading scores flavour. Almost nobody publishes a certificate of analysis for what is actually in the coffee.

The insight

Fermentation is not flavour decoration. It is molecular engineering.

Controlled fermentation changes which compounds survive into the cup and in what concentration. Treat it as a production variable rather than a regional tradition and coffee becomes something you can specify — the way a formulator specifies an ingredient.

01

Lots chosen for bioactive potential, not flavour score alone.

Batch-level testing for compound content and purity.

At origin — Colombia

The launch line — four protocols

Four processes. Four different molecules.

Each protocol is a distinct production route with a distinct target. Two further protocols — lactic-acid and triple-washed — stay in pipeline until the launch four have batch data behind them.

Protocol 01

Anaerobic

Cherries ferment in fully sealed, oxygen-deprived tanks. Removing oxygen changes which microbes dominate and how far fermentation runs.

Target · chlorogenic acid retention

Protocol 02

Alcohol-infused

Spirits introduce additional fermentable sugars that feed native yeasts, extending fermentation and building aromatic depth.

Target · aromatic complexity

Protocol 03

Flavour-infused

Natural botanicals introduced under controlled infusion produce pronounced fruit and berry expression without added flavourings.

Target · sensory differentiation

Protocol 04

Ultrasound-assisted extraction

Cavitation ruptures cell walls mechanically rather than thermally, releasing compounds in 60 min where conventional extraction takes 12 hrs.

Target · extraction yield & speed

Evidenced today

Honey processing is already in commercial trade.

Beans carrying mucilage through the drying stage — the honey process. Colita ships Black Honey and Yellow Honey lots today under its own export marks. Differentiated processing is not a plan here; it is a running operation.

Sealed-vessel anaerobic fermentation is the step still to be documented — in photographs and in laboratory data.

One structural question this deck must answer

Ultrasound-assisted extraction is an extraction technology, not a bean-processing one. It either produces a concentrated compound extract we sell or license, or it accelerates a step inside bean production. Those are two different companies with two different cost structures. The answer belongs on this page before the raise opens.

What already exists

Sensory QC runs. Instrumental analysis does not.

Colita already cups systematically — dozens of samples to the table, coded and scored. That is a real quality system and most producers do not have one.

But cupping measures flavour. It cannot measure chlorogenic acid. The gap is not rigour — it is instrument. The same discipline pointed at an HPLC is what turns every Target chip above into a result.

The distinction that decides the raise

The 25 cited studies establish what chlorogenic acid and coffee polyphenols do. They do not establish what Colita's coffee contains. Blending those two on one slide is the exact move that destroyed green-coffee credibility a decade ago. One honest COA on one protocol against one control is worth more to this raise than all four percentage figures.

Research / Coffee Chemistry

Beyond flavour: the chemistry inside coffee.

Colita's research programme follows the molecules, processing variables and extraction technologies that sit behind coffee quality — from chlorogenic acids and trigonelline to fermentation ecology and assisted extraction.

Human cohort

Imperial College London / EPIC

A 2017 European cohort of more than 500,000 people across 10 countries found higher coffee consumption was associated with lower all-cause mortality. The study was observational: it establishes an association, not proof that coffee causes longer life.

Imperial College London · Annals of Internal Medicine · 2017

Emerging biology

Trigonelline → NAD+ pathway

Nature Metabolism research in 2024 identified trigonelline as an NAD+ precursor through the NAPRT-dependent Preiss–Handler pathway. Human associations were paired with experiments in primary muscle cells, mice and C. elegans.

Nature Metabolism · 2024 · research evidence, not a Colita product claim

Longevity model

Trigonelline & lifespan research

A 2021 C. elegans study reported approximately 17.9% lifespan extension at the tested trigonelline condition and implicated AMPK, DAF-16/FOXO and HSF-1 signalling. This was a worm model, not a human longevity trial.

Preclinical model · 2021

Coffee chemistry

Green coffee bioactives

Published green-Arabica research has measured substantial natural variation in chlorogenic acids, trigonelline and caffeine. That makes origin, variety and processing relevant not only to flavour, but also to the molecular starting material.

Research range: CGAs 3.29–7.73%; trigonelline 0.53–1.27%; caffeine 0.78–1.55% dry mass in one 2024 Arabica dataset

Extraction R&D

Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction (UAE)

UAE uses acoustic cavitation and microstreaming to increase mass transfer. Coffee studies have investigated recovery of chlorogenic acid, trigonelline, caffeine and caffeic acid while controlling time, temperature, particle size and solvent system.

R&D route · parameters and yields must be validated lot by lot

Research frontier

More than CGA

Our watchlist includes 5-CQA and other CGA isomers, trigonelline, caffeine, caffeic acid, cafestol, kahweol, tocopherols, minor methylxanthines and coffee polysaccharides. Roasting also creates compounds such as melanoidins — coffee chemistry is transformed, not simply "destroyed" by heat.

Measure first. Claim second.

Commercial Platform / One Bean

One bean. Multiple revenue paths.

The green bean is not a single finished product. Selection, processing, format and extraction create several distinct commercial routes from the same coffee knowledge base.

Core

Curated green lots

Traceable coffees selected for quality, provenance, variety and buyer fit — supplied as green coffee for specialty customers.

Core

Made-to-order coffee

Buyers define a sensory direction; we design the processing and fermentation route around the target rather than asking them to choose only from a fixed catalogue.

Core

Fermentation development

Controlled and prolonged fermentation protocols developed around origin, coffee material and desired cup profile.

Format

Ground & finished formats

Coffee can move downstream into ground and convenience formats where the commercial brief requires a consumer-ready product.

Development

Bioactive extracts

Research into standardised coffee-derived extracts centred on chlorogenic acids, trigonelline and the wider green-coffee molecular matrix.

Development

Molecular fractions

Potential CGA-rich, trigonelline-rich and controlled-caffeine fractions, subject to process validation, analytical specification and regulatory review.

Development

Natural caffeine recovery

Extraction and fractionation can create more than one useful stream. Recovered coffee caffeine is being assessed as part of the whole-bean value model.

Future

Process IP & licensing

Validated fermentation and extraction protocols may create licensable know-how, private-development work and technology partnerships.
